dedicated.story:
"If we each only have one wing, why don't we just join them together to make a pair?"

Branze comforted a despondent Bransel, who saw himself and his brother as monsters for each having only one, extremely disparate-looking, wing. Branze urged Bransel not to put so much stock in others' opinions and to highlight their uniqueness instead, suggesting that they combine their individual wings to form a complete pair. Upon reaffirming the bond that allowed them to complement each other's deficiencies, the two brothers exchanged a smile.

lore:
Branze and Bransel look like children around twelve or thirteen years old, but their true ages are difficult to determine because they're half celestial and half demonkin.
The twins suddenly appeared one day in Telus, with their origins unknown.
In Telus, celestials do not exist, and are written of only in the ancient texts.
Their unexpected arrival caused a stir, and they were quickly captured and taken to a secret laboratory.
Since the twins held vague memories of the Celestial Realm, Black magicians and scientists were eager to obtain information from them and subjected them to countless experiments.
However, their small frames belied an immense power, making the experiments difficult to conduct. Eventually, they were made to live with several seals and restraints.
As a side effect of the countless experiments they were subjected to, they lost most of their memories.
They actually don't appear to have any painful memories at all.

When the dimensional walls of Telus collapsed and creatures from beyond began their invasion, the lab lost power. The twins' restraints weakened, and they escaped.
In the chaos, they slew every black magician and scientist who'd tormented them.
The creatures completely destroyed the lab, leaving no trace of Branze and Bransel's existence.

The twins were lost, starving, and on the brink of collapse when Platin found them. He took them in, and they lived at the temple with him.
However, since their wild natures often get the better of them, they can be impulsive, impatient, and chaotic... And they have the strength to throw around an axe heavier than anything a grown man could lift like a mere toy. Many accidents followed.
The people treated them like monsters.
Thankfully, any time something happened, Platin always stood by them, using his high status to shield them from punishment.
Because of his care, the twins are deeply attached to him.

Though they never shy away from a fight, the twins do not enjoy war, so they haven't intervened except for in the inevitable battles to protect the temple.
But everything changed when Pallanus detonated a dimensional vibration bomb, destroying the temple. The twins were grief-stricken, furious, and left without a home.
After Platin told them that they'd be able to use the Power of Destruction from another world to revive Telus and rebuild the temple, they joined the Dark Knights.
But when they discovered that Pallanus, the leader of the Dark Knights, was also the person that destroyed the temple, they became more interested in making trouble than performing their duties as members of the Dark Knights.
